thread.title: Apple's Deal For Peanuts Brings Spotlight To Small Cap DHX Media - DHX Media Ltd Variable Voting (NASDAQ:DHXM)

author: Chris Katje
title: Apple's Deal For Peanuts Brings Spotlight To Small Cap DHX Media - DHX Media Ltd Variable Voting (NASDAQ:DHXM)
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) announced recently that it was partnering with DHX Media ( DHXM ) to bring new original content based on the Peanuts brand to its soon to be launched streaming service. The deal marks a continuation of Apple’s billions of dollars strategy to create original content for its streaming service, which is expected to launch in 2019. For DHX, this is the announcement that was hinted at on recent calls to expand the Peanuts brand. Taking a deep look at DHX Media reveals an undervalued media company that should thrive for years to come in the era of subscription video on demand.
DHX Media is “a leading independent children’s content and brands company”. The Canadian company has well-known brands like Peanuts, Teletubbies, Strawberry Shortcake, Yo Gabba Gabba!, Degrassi, Inspector Gadget, and Cailou. The company holds the world’s largest independent kids’ content library with over 13,000 half hours of content. The company is a major content supplier to many of the top subscription services like Netflix, Amazon, Hulu, and others. Around 85% of the company’s distribution revenue comes from digital sources.
DHX is set to develop and produce original series, specials, and shorts based on the Peanuts brand for Apple. DHX will also create an exclusive to Apple short-form series with a focus on STEM themes for kids (science, technology, engineering, mathematics). DHX owns 41% of the Peanuts brand.
Before we dive into the bull case for DHX Media, it’s important to see that this deal is also important for Apple and its push into original programming. Apple’s CEO Tim Cook has put an emphasis on creating PG rated content and a focus on families. The company is spending around $5 billion this year to create original shows that will likely launch with the new Apple streaming service in 2019.
Apple has shelled out big bucks and signed big actors and directors to deals. Names like Jennifer Aniston, Reese Witherspoon, M. Night Shyamalan, J.J. Abrams, Damien Chazelle, Kevin Durant, and Steven Spielberg are all attached to projects at Apple. MacWorld has a good breakdown of projects being created for Apple.
Apple will likely highlight its streaming plans at a company event in 2019. Peanuts could become a focal point of that. What’s to stop Apple from creating a STEM based Peanuts show and then using this as a way to promote its iPad as a learning device for children. The deal with Peanuts content also comes after Apple signed a deal with Sesame Workshop to create content. The Sesame Workshop deal includes multiple series spanning live action, animation, and a new puppet series, but will not include the popular Sesame Street show, which airs on PBS and HBO.
As a parent myself, I can’t stress enough how important it is for streaming services to offer strong libraries of kids content. Apple is in the early stages of its own platform that will compete with Netflix, Hulu, and a new Disney offering. Signing Sesame Workshop and Peanuts to deals is a strong start and a possible way to lure parents and kids into using its products, especially if this content comes free.
According to CNBC , Apple plans to give away original content to device owners. Free original content from Apple will be mixed in with the ability for users to access other media apps directly through the Apple TV app. Apple will likely operate with the free model for some time and monetize down the road with a subscription service to its content.
Down the road, Apple could combo its Apple Music, AppleTV, and Texture (digital magazines) services for one monthly price. Apple continues to see strength in subscription revenue and television should be a long-term driver for the company.
(Source: November Presentation )
DHX Media is a company that should benefit as companies push the limits in spending for library titles and new original content. A look at this chart shows how this amount has greatly increased. The deal with Apple strengthens this argument. DHX could have created original content for its own Canadian networks, its YouTube WildBrain channel, or another provider. However, it is likely that Apple provided a nice payment to strengthen its upcoming streaming option for customers and its push to include PG rated content to appeal to parents and children.
Take a look at how the company’s revenue mix has shifted thanks to the inclusion on Peanuts strong licensing and consumer products power.
(Source: November Presentation )
Back in November, DHX Media laid out three main priorities for fiscal 2019. They were:
Develop new, and revitalize classic brands with content on WildBrain Develop premium kids’ content to drive franchise brands Improve cash flow and balance sheet Under the develop premium kids’ content came the goal of “drive major agreements for Peanuts to grow brand exposure and licensee base”.
The company’s Peanuts brand received several of its own slides in the investor presentation. This should highlight just how important the brand is for the company and how important this new Apple deal is for the company and its short and long term success.
For investors who have followed the DHX story over the last two years, this marks the reveal that has been hinted at by the company for the new plans for Peanuts. On the first quarter earnings call , the company had this to say, “There are great many things happening with Peanuts. We can’t pull back the curtain on many of them just yet, but the team is busy working on a number of projects, including the development of new Peanuts content.”
(Source: November Presentation )
The slide above highlights the strength of the Peanuts brand on a global sale. The brand continues to be a strong licensing powerhouse with $1.3 billion in annual retail sales. More than 1100 licensees use Peanuts characters across segments like clothing, theme parks, and insurance. The deal with Apple should help bring in additional licensees as the brand becomes top of mind for kids and consumers thanks to the newly created content. The focus on STEM education and NASA partnership could shift Peanuts into the growing STEM toys and kids educational toy markets. Also keep in mind that this Peanuts deal comes after some were worried about losing the reported $12 million that Peanuts received annually from MetLife to be used in advertising.
DHX Media acquired an 80% stake in the Peanuts brand, along with 100% of the Strawberry Shortcake brand, back in 2017. The company paid $345 million to Iconix Brand Group ( ICON ) for the stake. The Charles Schulz family owned the remaining 20% of Peanuts at the time of the sale. Since that time, DHX Media entered a new agreement to sell a portion of its stake to Sony ( SNE ).
DHX Media recognized $161 million in net proceeds on the sale of the minority stake in Peanuts to Sony. Peanuts cost synergies are expected to be $5 million annually for the first couple of years and then increase to $25 million within five years.
There were several reasons to make the deal with Sony. DHX Media has used over $200 million to pay down debt, with much of that coming from the partial Peanuts sale. The deal with Sony also strengthened the Peanuts brand in Japan, where it was weaker. The Peanuts brand has seen 200% growth in revenue in Asia since 2010. Along with the Sony deal, DHX signed a deal with CAA Global for the Peanuts brand in China and other parts of Asia. This again strengthened the Peanuts brand in parts of the world where it was weaker. The Peanuts brand has seen 200% growth in revenue in Asia since 2010.
A look at the slide above shows part of the strategy for the Peanuts brand. On the left hand side shows the content side of things with short form, digital growth, and new series all as the strategy. The Apple deal should hit on all of these. The new series should also help with items in the other two columns like re-introducing specials, and global reach under distribution. On the third column of consumer products, DHX and investors should hope that the new series and specials leads to increased demand to license the Peanuts gang to new and expanded deals.
While DHX Media has other strong brands, Peanuts remains one of the companies top revenue drivers, as it touches several of the company’s segments and is the major reason that the consumer products segment has grown so much since the acquisition. The release of a Peanuts theatrical movie in 2015 was big for the Peanuts brand as it brought new viewers and new licensees into the fold. I would expect the same thing to happen here with new content and a strong partnership from Apple. I was surprised that shares have not moved on the news already for this small cap stock.
Another strong catalyst for DHX Media is its WildBrain segment. WildBrain is one of the largest networks of kids content on YouTube. The company continues to release staggering numbers for the growth at WildBrain. Total minutes viewed on YouTube increased to 129 billion in fiscal 2018, up from 55 billion the prior year. The channel has seen a 112% compound annual growth rate in total views over the last five years. Thanks to the growth of viewership, WildBrain is attracting premium advertising rates, which is helping WildBrain increase its overall revenue and contribution towards DHX Media as a whole.
(Source: November Presentation )
WildBrain revenue increased to $57.3 million in fiscal 2018. This was an increase from fiscal 2017’s $34.0 million. Over the last five years, revenue for WildBrain has increased at an average annual rate of 68%. The company reported recently that one in three kids with access to YouTube watched WildBrain content in the first quarter. That is a staggering statistic that should help WildBrain gain on the advertising front and also sign up more third party partners.
(Source: November Presentation )
In the first quarter , WildBrain saw 13 billion minutes of content watched on YouTube, up from 8 billion in the prior year. Revenue for WildBrain hit $16 million, up from $11 million in the prior year. As an example of the strength of WildBrain, DHX Media highlighted its Tiddlytubbies brand, which saw its originals watched 29 million times in the first quarter, versus 12 million in the fourth quarter.
Along with showcasing DHX Media’s own brands, WildBrain has had success producing original content for media companies and brands. The company has even partnered with toy brands to create content for YouTube to help promote the brands prior to a retail launch. WildBrain signed with Irish company The Fairy Door Company to help manage its social media strategies for YouTube and Facebook. WildBrain will produce short-form animated content, live-action content, and run advertising campaigns.
Aside from Peanuts and WildBrain, DHX Media continues to be one of the leading suppliers of content to Netflix and other SVODs. The company highlighted its new “Creeped Out” live action horror show that was delivered to Netflix and premiered in October. “The Deep”, an animated series on Netflix, will air its third season in 2019. A new animated preschool show called “Chip and Potato” will also premiere on Netflix in 2019. Another show the company sounded excited about was “Rev & Roll”, an animated show in collaboration with Alpha Group, a leading toy and animation company in China.
(Source: November Presentation )
Shares of DHX Media now trade at just over $2 a share in the United States. The company has shares listed in both Canada and the United States. Shares have traded between $0.80 and $2.80 over the last 52 weeks. The company has a market capitalization of under $500 million. I believe shares are significantly undervalued based on the recent Peanuts deal, the strength of WildBrain and the company’s huge content library, which will continue to be monetized going forward. Add up the sum of the parts and shares are likely worth double what they are now.
Interestingly enough, the company’s CEO Michael Donovan believes shares should trade north of $10 in the next few years. While every CEO would love to be bullish and say shares are undervalued, DHX Media’s CEO has a huge incentive to get shares there. The Board of Directors recently made his option calls start at $10 in 2025. The CEO now has five to six years to get shares to double digits. I expect shares to hit $5 by 2020 and think double digits could be well within reach if the current plan is maintained and new goals are laid out.
